quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can the body eliminate per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. The time it takes to lower your blood alcohol content (BAC) varies. It is safest not to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: The front tire provides power, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire will shake the bike and make mirrors hard to use.
You won't be able to use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects how you steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, exit the road safely as quickly as possible.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Give you a good view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your plans from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen, avoids surface hazards, avoids wind blasts from other vehicles, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: Use the brake throughout the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before turning.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: How should you apply your brakes?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes safely and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes safely and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes safely if you can. Speeding up will only encourage them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: What helmet gives you the most protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that has survived a previous crash.
A helmet that provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the most protection. Helmets should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol content (BAC) is a person legally intoxicated?
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding with this BAC level is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which will NOT reduce your chance of having an accident?

options.text: Spotting hazards and deciding what to handle first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide what to handle first. Always use your headlight to be more visible and keep plenty of space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best protection when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Distance is your best protection against crashes. Keep plenty of space between you and other vehicles so you have time to react to their mistakes. Wearing proper gear is also important.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down your body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
Your entire face, including your eyes.
Your face less well than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire face, including your eyes.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face and eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.

questions.question: What kind of sign is usually rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. These signs tell riders what rules to follow on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when wobbling—it makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not brake, as this may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Is lane sharing allowed?

options.text: Allowed if you have had your license for more than three years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not allowed.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane to operate safely, just like cars. Lane sharing is usually not allowed. Choose your lane position to keep others from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: How can you make yourself more visible while riding?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on all the time.
Ride on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on all the time.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothes, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What should you NOT do on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded spots, and bridges—these are more slippery.

questions.question: How do you maintain control while turning your motorcycle?

options.text: Look through the turn to see what is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle through a turn, look through it by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: How should you adjust your riding when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Follow other vehicles more closely than when riding alone.
Brake later than you would when riding alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra passenger weight means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start braking earlier, increase your following distance, and look for bigger gaps when crossing or merging.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have used their motorcycle for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Less than six months.
questions.explanation: Be very careful on a motorcycle that is new to you. Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay on your seat and lift your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down. Hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front end.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:
questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen in daylight when riders are traveling at low speeds.

questions.question: Motorcyclists in a group should avoid riding in pairs because:

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may make it hard for riders to see.
Riders do not have enough space to avoid hazards.
It is too difficult for riders on the left to exit the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders do not have enough space to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, do not ride in pairs. Each rider will not have enough room to maneuver and avoid hazards.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: Slower than during the day under similar conditions.
At the same speed as during the day under similar conditions.
Faster than during the day under similar conditions.
On the shoulder of the road so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than during the day under similar conditions.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, travel slower than you would during the day in similar weather and traffic. It is harder to see hazards in the dark, so slower speeds help you avoid them.
